name: ID-02
label: Likely R

key_factors: District's R+13 partisan lean in deeply Republican eastern Idaho
Simpson's roughly 8-to-1 fundraising advantage and incumbency
Prediction market prices Democratic win odds near 4%
No public polling, leaving fundamentals to carry the forecast
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: the district leans Republican by thirteen points, Mike Simpson is a long-serving incumbent who has raised over $1.3 million to Ellie Gilbreath's $161,000, and prediction markets give Democrats only about a 4% chance. With no polls or outside spending to complicate the picture, the expected margin sits around Republican plus fifteen to sixteen points.
model.watch: A sharp national shift against Republicans or an unexpected scandal involving Simpson could narrow the race, though even a strong wave would likely leave the seat favored to stay Republican.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mike Simpson, a longtime Republican incumbent, is heavily favored in this eastern Idaho district, which leans Republican by thirteen points. He has raised about $1.3 million and holds a large cash advantage over Democrat Ellie Gilbreath, who has brought in roughly $161,000 and has no outside support on either side. Minor-party and Libertarian candidates are on the ballot but are barely funded.

There is no public polling of the general election, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive. Prediction markets give Democrats about a 4% chance of an upset. The most likely outcome is a comfortable Simpson victory in the mid-teens, consistent with the district's fundamentals and the absence of any evidence of a genuine contest.
